reasons.reader_question: Meera's 'After that it's only you' clearly sets the question: will Ila keep the map promise once the mountain stops enforcing it?
reasons.change: Raghu goes from armed hunter to prisoner, the keepers' location is known, and the leads move from hunted to declared and free.
reasons.romance_movement: The declaration is new: she says it in the light so he can see her hands, and adds a promise that costs her oath.
reasons.shown_chemistry: The pencil leads, unbuttoning with palms, and 'use your mouth and I'll tell you the shape' are responsive acts tied to these two people.
reasons.character_logic: Kunal's use of the rope rule is sharp. One slip: he believes Raghu because of a Pasang report that hasn't been given yet.
reasons.stakes_and_cost: The promise costs the crown oath and the audit, and Pasang gives up his captain. Kunal declines to promise what he can't deliver.
reasons.prose: Clean, concrete and varied, with no banned phrases. A few murky lines: 'This time the blade was only true'; the age insertion is a little blunt.
reasons.continuity: Consistent with F795, F610, F409 and F777. The morning timing is ambiguous against 'Day sixteen' but does not clearly conflict.

fixes: At 'It fitted too well to be a boy's invention', Kunal relies on Pasang's winter-way report before Pasang has made it (character logic, sequencing). Either move Pasang's 'The way was for the regent Pritam and the men waiting on him' ahead of this line, or base Kunal's belief on the Sarn fold detail alone.

At '"He went home," said Raghu. "Walking."': in ch 29 Ila relied on the vault being a cairn whose stones ring at a lie, yet here they stay silent (technique 22 underused). Have the seams brighten and the stones ring high as Raghu lies. This gives Pasang an instrument he can't argue with, alongside the grey knuckles.

At 'Kunal woke with the sun on the boards', it is unclear whether this is the same day or the next morning, while Meera says 'Day sixteen' (risk of drift from F795). State that it is late morning of the same day. Also make the final image push forward: have Meera add one fact that makes ch 31 necessary, such as the queen's riders on the road.
reader_question: When the bond ends at the Meadow Cairn, will Ila keep a promise the mountain no longer enforces?
new_facts_assessment: F805 is consistent and necessary, but its reasoning depends on Pasang's winter-way report, which comes later on the page; fix the order. F806 matches F622 and F795 (35-day bond, Shilak council three weeks later) and usefully sets up the book's question.
